items.followUp: How many bits are there in 3 bytes?

rubric.why: Shows that a bit is a single binary digit.
rubric.description: Defines a bit as one binary digit.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a bit represents one binary digit or one of the values 0 and 1.

rubric.why: Gives the standard size of a byte.
rubric.description: States that one byte consists of eight bits.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a byte as a group of eight bits.

modelAnswer: A bit is the smallest unit of data and represents one binary digit, 0 or 1.
A byte is a group of 8 bits.

items.followUp: What is phishing, and how can a user avoid it?

rubric.why: Identifies the demand that characterizes advance fee fraud.
rubric.description: States that the victim is asked to pay a fee in advance.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning an upfront fee or advance payment.

rubric.why: Explains the false promise used to deceive the victim.
rubric.description: States that payment is requested in return for money, a prize, a loan, or another promised benefit that is not delivered.
rubric.how: Award for explaining the promised benefit and that it is fraudulent or never provided.

modelAnswer: Advance fee fraud is a scam in which a victim is asked to pay an upfront fee to receive a promised reward, loan, or large sum of money.
The promised benefit is not delivered, and the fraudster keeps the fee.

items.followUp: What is plagiarism, and why is it considered unethical?

rubric.why: Explains the purpose of copyright law.
rubric.description: States that copyright law provides legal protection to creators.
rubric.how: Award for describing legal protection of creative work or its creator.

rubric.why: Identifies the rights copyright grants or controls.
rubric.description: Mentions the creator's rights to control use, copying, or distribution of the work.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the law gives creators control over copying, distributing, or using their work.

modelAnswer: Copyright law is the law that gives creators legal protection for their original work.
It gives them control over how their work is copied, distributed, or used.

items.followUp: Name two types of transmission media used in computer networks.

rubric.why: States the main function of a transmission medium.
rubric.description: Explains that a transmission medium carries data or signals.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is used to carry or transmit information.

rubric.why: Identifies where the data is carried.
rubric.description: States that data travels between connected devices.
rubric.how: Award for referring to communication between devices or network nodes.

modelAnswer: A transmission medium is used to carry data or signals from one device to another.
It provides the communication path between devices in a network.

items.followUp: What is a router, and what is its role in a network?

rubric.why: Identifies the information routing handles on the Internet.
rubric.description: States that routing deals with forwarding data packets.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning packets or data packets.

rubric.why: Explains how routing delivers data across networks.
rubric.description: States that routers direct packets toward their destination by selecting a suitable path.
rubric.how: Award for describing direction toward the destination or path selection by routers.

modelAnswer: Routing on the Internet is the process of forwarding data packets from a source to their destination.
Routers choose a suitable path for the packets as they travel between networks.

items.followUp: Which HTML tags are used to create a table row and a table cell?

rubric.why: Explains the purpose of an HTML table.
rubric.description: States that an HTML table organizes or displays information in a structured form.
rubric.how: Award for describing the table's purpose.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic structure of a table.
rubric.description: States that table information is arranged in rows and columns.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning rows and columns.

modelAnswer: Making a table in HTML means arranging information in a structured form using HTML table elements.
The information is organized into rows and columns.

items.followUp: What is a website, and how is it different from a web page?

rubric.why: Identifies what a web page is.
rubric.description: Defines a web page as a document available on the World Wide Web.
rubric.how: Award for calling it a document or page on the web.

rubric.why: Describes how a web page is accessed.
rubric.description: States that it can be opened or viewed using a browser, usually through its address.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning access through a browser or a web address.

modelAnswer: A web page is a document available on the World Wide Web.
It can be viewed using a web browser, usually by entering its URL.

items.followUp: Describe bus topology and ring topology, including one feature of each.

rubric.why: Identifies the central connection used in a star topology.
rubric.description: States that each device in a star topology connects to a central hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the central connecting device.

rubric.why: Adds a valid feature of star topology.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant feature, such as easy addition of devices or that failure of the central hub can disrupt the network.
rubric.how: Award for one accurate feature or consequence of star topology.

rubric.why: Describes the interconnections in mesh topology.
rubric.description: States that each device is directly connected to every other device in a full mesh.
rubric.how: Award for explaining the direct connections among devices.

rubric.why: Adds a valid feature of mesh topology.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant feature, such as reliability, alternative paths, or the cost and cabling required.
rubric.how: Award for one accurate advantage or disadvantage of mesh topology.

modelAnswer: In star topology, every device is connected to a central hub or switch.
It is easy to add devices, but failure of the central hub can stop communication across the network.
In mesh topology, each device is directly connected to every other device.
Mesh topology is reliable because alternative paths may be available, but it requires many connections and is costly.
